questions.q: In the real ATM analogy from this lesson, what causes the machine to keep giving out money repeatedly?
options: The machine hasn't finished updating your balance before you press withdraw again
The ATM ran out of cash
questions.explain: The analogy captures the real mechanism: repeatedly triggering a withdrawal before the balance update ever completes lets you keep withdrawing more than you should.

questions.q: What real Solidity feature makes reentrancy attacks possible?
options: Fallback functions, which can contain arbitrary logic and trigger automatically when ETH arrives
questions.explain: A fallback function fires automatically when ETH is sent with no matching function call — and since it can contain arbitrary logic, an attacker can hide malicious re-entry code there.

questions.q: What real, concrete flaw in the DAO's contract allowed the attack to succeed?
options: It sent ETH to a caller before updating that caller's recorded balance
It had no functions at all
It used too high a compiler version
It stored no data on the blockchain
questions.explain: Because the balance update happened after sending ETH, the attacker's fallback function could call withdraw again and again while the balance check kept passing.

questions.q: What real, lasting consequence did the community's response to the DAO hack produce?
options: A hard fork that split Ethereum into two separate real blockchains — Ethereum and Ethereum Classic
The permanent shutdown of the Ethereum network
A ban on all future smart contracts
No real consequence — the hack was quietly ignored
questions.explain: The contested decision to reverse the theft via a hard fork produced two real, still-existing chains: Ethereum (post-fork) and Ethereum Classic (the original, unaltered chain).

questions.q: What was the real total value drained in the DAO hack, per this lesson?
options: Roughly 150 million dollars' worth of ETH
questions.explain: The DAO had raised about $150 million worth of ETH from investors, and a large portion of that was drained by the real attacker.
